correctness.rationale: The integer-slope modular congruence lemma gives exactly D^n−1 phase-shifted grid solutions; nested application in z,y,x proves the all-period product independently of Borel forcing. Finite periodic sets permit exact Möbius inversion and formal zeta algebra. Successive Fubini reductions show volume invariance. Conditional grid quadrature proves the beta/2 sum reciprocal-count Wasserstein bound for every 1-Lipschitz observable, and the zero-shift z-observable proves optimal exponential order when E is minimal. An exact-rational checker confirms three nontrivial polynomial instances for n=1,2,3 and verifies direct returns, one discontinuous Borel forcing instance, and the sharp example; proof, not finite checks, carries infinite statements.

originality.rationale: The primary full text (Zhang et al. 2023, DOI 10.3390/e25071005) proves triangular Lyapunov-exponent claims rather than an exact all-period census or finite-time periodic equidistribution. Puri–Ward 2001 gives only general orbit-count inversion, and Chothi–Everest–Ward 1997 deals with algebraic-group endomorphisms, not arbitrary Borel triangular couplings. Searches for alias forms, stronger skew-product counting results and exact parameter tables did not find a stated theorem implying the coupling-independent fixed grid structure together with the uniform beta/2 sum 1/(D^n−1) Wasserstein bound; unindexed literature and unread older full texts remain priority risks.

value.rationale: The motivating 2023 system proposes a tunable three-dimensional polynomial modular map and evaluates its output statistically using finite samples. On its natural deterministic integer-slope regime, the theorem yields a full primitive-cycle census, exact rational zeta, Haar invariance and forcing-uniform quantitative periodic-point distribution for every period with optimal exponential order. These are meaningful global invariants that cannot be inferred from source Lyapunov exponents or numerical histograms. It makes no cryptographic security or out-of-scope stochastic claim.
